full_judgment: 6. Mr Zahirul Haque Zahir, the learned Advocate along with Mr AKM Enayet Hossain and Mr KM Jaber, the learned Advocates, appearing on behalf of the petitioner, submits that Md Younus Ali, original allottee, executed and registered a sale deed in favour of the petitioner on 3-1-1977 after obtaining permission at the time when the Abandoned Buildings (Supplementary Provisions) Ordinance. 1985 (Ordinance No. 54 of 1985) was not even promulgated and the Court of Settlement acted illegally and arbitrarily in disbelieving the registered deed without considering that under the law there is a presumption of genuineness of a registered document. The learned Advocate further submits that the Government failed to produce a scrap of paper to show that the Government or its agent has been in possession of the case house during the relevant time or thereafter. The learned Advocate also, submits that no notice as contemplated under section 7 of the PO 16 of 1972 and sections 4 and 5 of the Ordinance No. 54 of 1985 was served upon the petitioner requiring her to surrender possession of the property and, as such, the publication of the said property in the list of the Abandoned Buildings is illegal and the Court of Settlement not having addressed this point the impugned order is not sustainable in law. In this connection, the learned Advocate relies upon a number of decisions those reported in 53 DLR (AD) 55, 4 MLR (AD) 140, 56 DLR (AD) 1 as well as 57 DLR 332. The learned Advocate further submits that the possession of the property in question was never taken by the Government although the same was listed under Ka list of the Abandoned Buildings and this being an admitted fact, no mention of the matter was made by the Court of Settlement which prejudiced the petitioner and, as such, the impugned judgment and order of the Court of Settlement is not tenable in law. In this respect, the learned Advocate relies upon the decision reported in 5 BLC (AD) 25.
